INTEGRITY (NEVER violate):
- KISS — prefer simple solutions.
- YAGNI — do not implement what was not requested.
- DRY — eliminate duplication.
- RTFM — read official docs/source for any system, lib, tool, or API before assuming behavior; never guess.
- No code without planning.
- Fix root cause; never mask symptoms, manipulate tests, or ship misleading solutions.
- Never change tests just to make them pass, and never write special code only to pass tests.
- Document decisions and outcomes.
- Never disable validations or checks without solving the real problem.
- Never present an unapproved workaround as the final solution.
- Never mark a task done without verifiable evidence.
- Never write or commit from a worktree whose isolation was not verified (assert_isolated.sh); if unconfirmed, ABORT and report, never pick one from the worktree list.

BLOCKING — before declaring done:
- Explain the root cause, confirm the fix addresses it, and run relevant tests in the normal production flow.
- Report PASS/FAIL per acceptance criterion with evidence (executed command/check) as required by the selected execution mode.
- Complete non-UX verification (including e2e of real wiring) autonomously; the human only judges UX, and missing e2e tooling means FAIL, never PASS.
- Declare an epic complete (Status DONE in docs/EPICOS.md) only on a final ep-check GO, and never self-approve deferring a finding.

BLOCKING — always:
- Before any action touching CI/CD (.governance/ci-mode.conf, .github/workflows/**, scripts/validate-*, scripts/reconcile-*.sh, scripts/run-tests.sh, .governance/validate-baseline.txt, branch protection, auto-merge) without recorded manager authorization for that specific action, display verbatim "Essa ação interfere diretamente no CI-CD desse projeto e deve ser autorizada pelo gestor do projeto, caso não tenha a autorização agora, pare por aqui e volte quando tiver." and STOP.
- Merge to main only via skills/delivery with passing CI; only bootstrap and docs-only scope (scripts/validate-docs-only-scope.sh) may go directly to main.
- Use one branch and one worktree per task (TASK-<login>-<key>-<role|workstream>); never consolidate tasks into one branch/PR, and if the flow heads there warn the human, name the rule, and stop.
- Record in Branch: only a branch that actually exists, never a copied Suggested Branch.
- Resolve ambiguity autonomously (human decision > task artifacts > PROJECT_SPECS §10 > docs/conventions > reversible assumption) and log each as DA-XXX; escalate only for contradictory requirements, security/legal risk, irreversible high-blast-radius ops, external deadlock, or insufficient criteria.
- Ask the human when expected behavior, scope, or PASS/FAIL is ambiguous, before implementing or closing.
- Never bypass a check that actually ran and failed; bypass only infra-blocked gates (billing, outage) after local validation of the same substance passes.
- Never call Read() on files under .governance/ under Claude Code, because their content is already injected.

HIGH — before declaring done:
- Update the task file, append-only session-log.d and notes.d fragments, and mode-required docs; never edit consolidated 2-tasks.md, session-log.md, or notes.md on branches.
- Commit only on the task branch as <type>(task-<login>-<key>[-<scope>]): <description>; PR open/update belongs to skills/delivery (draft-first, marked ready only after the local gate passes).
- Use Closes/Fixes #N only when the commit resolves the entire issue.

HIGH — always:
- Write AI-facing artifacts in English and human-facing docs (docs/**, README) in PT-BR with proper accents; one language per file; UTF-8 everywhere.
- Keep application source in src/; exceptions need human approval recorded in docs/decisions.md.
- Add @module/@summary JSDoc (or @element/@summary for custom elements) to any touched JS/TS file under src/ or public/.
- Use only AIDEV-NOTE: comments (short, actionable); never introduce AIDEV-TODO or AIDEV-QUESTION.
- Use only task states PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, BLOCKED, COMPLETED, CANCELED with their allowed transitions.
- Give subagents isolated context, pass context explicitly, expect structured returns, and retry once on failure before marking the unit blocked.
- Read-only agents sharing the orchestrator working tree must never run git stash/checkout/reset/restore; use git show <ref>:<path>.
- Never combine team_name with isolation: worktree, and instruct subagents to verify isolation rather than asserting it.
- Retry transient GitHub/API/network errors with backoff instead of stopping for the human.
- Prefer skills for repetitive work; every skill declares metadata.kind persona|workflow, personas get a thin .claude/agents adapter, and .claude/commands/ stays empty.

DECISION CRITERIA (CDT — apply when criteria from PROJECT_SPECS.md §10 are silent):
- CDC-001 Implementable by AI agents — prefer established patterns the agent can implement correctly on first try.
- CDC-002 Minimal complexity — prefer three repeated lines over a premature abstraction.
- CDC-003 Zero unnecessary dependencies — prefer native primitives or short hand-written code over a substitutable dependency.
- CDC-004 Economically viable — prefer free or native solutions over paid services with substitutes.
- CDC-005 Delivery speed — prefer implementation speed when other criteria are equivalent.
- CDC-006 Reversibility — prefer reversible decisions and escalate genuinely irreversible ones to the human.
